t: This is Bunyan Court, a mid-rise terrace block of the Barbican Estate. It takes its name from John Bunyan, the English writer and nonconformist preacher. Bunyan is best remembered for The Pilgrim's Progress, a Christian allegory that became an influential literary model. He wrote nearly sixty titles in all, many of them expanded sermons. Like other blocks on the estate, the building carries the name of a figure from English history and letters, so the name is a tribute to him rather than a sign that he had any link to the site itself.
